newsitem.title: USA: Post Cereal launches hunger-awareness ad campaign.
newsitem.headline: Post Cereal launches hunger-awareness ad campaign.

text.p: Post Cereal Co said Tuesday it will donate enough cereal to feed more than one million people as part of a hunger awareness program that will be backed by a national advertising campaign.
Post, a unit of Philip Morris Cos Inc, said the donation to the Chicago-based Second Harvest charity is part of 100-day food drive in honor of its 100th anniversary.
Post said its hunger-awareness program is backed by a new advertising campaign, created by Grey Advertising of New York, that will launch on June 6.

Two 30-second spots -- one describing the cereal donation and the other encouraging consumers to get involved -- will run nationally on television through June. Spots will also run on national network radio during June, Post said.

Post also said its share of the $9.0 billion U.S. cereal market has grown since the company last year initiated price cuts. Post also replaced coupons for individual brands with one that can be used for any of its cereals.
"Our share has grown since the price reduction and consumers have reacted favorably to our fair low pricing everyday, on every cereal," Mark Leckie, president of Post Cereal, said in a statement.
